senses.gloss: f. (נָזַף) anger, rebuke, esp. n’zifah, a lower degree of excommunication; v. נִידּוּי.
units: <cite ref="Sanhedrin 68a:2">Snh. 68ᵃ</cite> <he>גער בו ויצא בנ׳</he> he frowned at him, and he (the son) went away feeling the rebuke.
<cite ref="Shabbat 31a:5">Sabb. 31ᵃ</cite> <he>והוציאו בנ׳</he> and made him go out in anger.
<cite ref="Shabbat 97a:3">Ib. 97ᵃ</cite> <he>ההוא בנ׳ בעלמא</he> this (<he>בם</he>, <cite ref="Numbers 12:9">Num. XII, 9</cite>) refers only to the anger (of the Lord, not to leprosy).
<cite ref="Moed Katan 16a:20">M. Kat. 16ᵃ</cite> <he>אין נ׳ פחות וכ׳</he> the minor ban lasts no less than seven days.
Ib. 16ᵇ נ׳ דידהו their (the Palestinian) n’zifah; נ׳ דידן our (the Babylonian) n.; a. fr.
